alternatives_considered: Potential RFP to other RCM vendors (e.g., eClinicalWorks, NextGen)
battlecards.why_selected: Retaining athenaOne avoided a $9M early-termination penalty while securing market-aligned 3.15 % fee and retroactive credits.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year addendum effective 9/1/2022 with 3.15 % of collections, retroactive pricing credit, option to extend to 5 years.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Benchmark data showed fees 25–40 bps above market; Advantia threatened RFP and migration to Collector to secure concessions.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Integrated EHR/RCM platform, minimal transition risk, proven performance metrics.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Historically high rates, onerous termination penalty, limited pricing flexibility without pressure.
battlecards.switching_costs: Estimated $9 M contract penalty plus system conversion and user retraining.
battlecards.notes: Savings scenario based on $110 M annual collections tier.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided best-and-final pricing across 9,000 SKUs, agreed to 60-day terms and dedicated implementation resources for Heartland clinics.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year prime-vendor agreement with formulary compliance, QBRs, and ≤3 % annual price-cap; enterprise‐wide scope.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggregated Heartland + Mid-Atlantic volumes and multi-supplier RFP created price tension.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Nationwide distribution network, robust reporting, ability to support implementation team.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher minimum order quantities than regional distributors; some specialty items sourced via third parties.
battlecards.switching_costs: Clinic staff training on new ordering platform and SKU conversions; moderate but manageable.
battlecards.notes: McKesson retained Mid-Atlantic business and captured Heartland business previously with Medline.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Could not match McKesson’s BAFO pricing or extend payment terms; limited value-added services relative to peers.
battlecards.contract_terms: Prior Heartland distributor agreement – annual renewals, 30-day terms.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Loss of Heartland volume reduced Medline’s scale advantage.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Strong private-label offering, historical relationship in Heartland.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Pricing uncompetitive, lacked enterprise implementation team.
battlecards.switching_costs: SKU cross-references and inventory run-down in Heartland sites.
battlecards.notes: Heartland locations migrated to McKesson effective 10/31/22.

battlecards.why_selected: Operational continuity (embedded phlebotomists, LIS interfaces) outweighed incremental savings from switching to Quest.
battlecards.contract_terms: Repriced test menu effective 11/1/2022; 2-year rate lock with CPI ≤2 % escalator.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Quest BAFO priced 16 % below incumbent, creating credible switch threat.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Existing integrations, staff in clinics, acceptable revised pricing.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Legacy pricing was 10 % above market; limited flexibility prior to RFQ.
battlecards.switching_costs: Re-interfacing LIS, retraining staff, potential patient disruption.
battlecards.notes: Advantia may revisit Quest option if service issues arise.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Changeover risk (phlebotomy staffing, specimen logistics) deemed too high relative to incremental savings.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Used as competitive benchmark to pressure LabCorp pricing.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Lowest BAFO pricing across top 50 CPTs; strong national footprint.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: No existing integration, transition effort required for 24 Mid-Atlantic sites.
battlecards.switching_costs: Systems interface build, staff transition, payer notification.
battlecards.notes: Advantia kept Quest proposal on file for future cycles.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Per-scan pricing 20 % above market; would not align to perm-hire conversion model.
battlecards.contract_terms: Practice-specific month-to-month agreements at $50 per scan.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to hire sonographers directly and supplement with agency reduced vendor’s leverage.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Simple variable pricing, no fixed overhead.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: High unit cost, limited talent pipeline, inconsistent scheduling.
battlecards.switching_costs: Minimal—knowledge transfer to newly hired staff and credentialing.
battlecards.notes: Service terminated progressively as in-house hires ramped up (completion by EOY 2022).

battlecards.why_selected: Provides flexible 20 % coverage while internal recruiter builds pipeline; lowest markup among staffing agencies contacted.
battlecards.contract_terms: 12-month master services agreement; markup capped at 22 % over wage; cancel with 30-day notice.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Agency motivated by long-term growth as Advantia expands footprint.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Scalable sourcing capability, healthcare recruiting expertise.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher hourly rate than direct hire; performance dependent on recruiter quality.
battlecards.notes: Expected to cover ~20 % of scans during transition year.

summary.skipped_reason: Suppliers in IUD purchasing, Bayer replacement program, office supplies, telecom and IT managed services lacked finalized negotiations or only involved minor policy changes.
